summary: This RFC defines Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP) packages for voiceband data, such as fax or modem tones sent over a voice call. They let a Call Agent authorize and monitor a connection switching to and from voiceband data mode, with or without redundancy and forward error correction. A companion general-purpose media parameter package is also defined.

eli5.summary: Phone lines can carry fax squeals as well as voices. This gives the phone system boss a way to say when a call may switch to carrying those squeals, and to keep watch while it happens.

questions: how to authorize fax over mgcp
subtitle: Protocol extensions to detect and control fax and modem tones over voice calls.

tldr.problem: When a voice call switches to modem or fax data, a media gateway needs to detect this change and coordinate it with a call control server. Existing gateway control protocols do not provide a standard way to authorize such transitions or monitor them in progress.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines two packages for the Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP): a VBD package that lets a call agent authorize and monitor transitions to voiceband data mode, and a General-Purpose Media Descriptor package for additional codec modes. The packages define events that occur when VBD is detected (gwvbd, nopvbd) and optional parameters for coordination technique, codec, direction, and reason codes.
tldr.outcome: Call servers can now authorize and track modem, fax, and text transmissions over VoIP connections with or without redundancy and forward error correction (FEC), allowing reliable data transmission over voice codecs.

today: RFC 6498 is an Informational specification and remains the standard for controlling voiceband data transitions in MGCP gateways. It is not obsoleted and is used in telecommunications systems that need to support modem and fax transmission over IP networks with MGCP control.

sections.title: Introduction to Voiceband Data
sections.content:
Voiceband Data (VBD) refers to using a voice codec such as G.711u or G.711a to carry data payloads over RTP. This allows modems and fax machines to operate over IP networks by modulating their signals as audio. A voice call between two endpoints may switch to VBD mode when modem or fax tones are detected, allowing data transmission without changing the underlying media codec.

The RFC covers multiple VBD procedures, each with different coordination techniques. Some use mutually negotiated methods via SDP (Session Description Protocol), such as ITU-T V.150.1 State Signaling Events or V.152 Payload Type Switching. Others do not require negotiation: the gateway detects tones directly, or the IP side sends VBD-encoded RTP packets. RFC 4733 and RFC 4734 can convey fax and modem events as DTMF-like telephone events.

MGCP packages extend the Media Gateway Control Protocol to authorize and monitor these transitions on behalf of a Call Agent (the call control server).
sections.eli5: Phone calls use voice codec to send sound. Fax and modems send special sounds too. This RFC explains how the phone system can detect when a call is switching to those special sounds and keep track of it.

sections.title: VBD Packages and Events
sections.content:
The RFC defines two MGCP packages. The VBD package (vbd) defines events for two complementary VBD procedures. The Gateway Controlled VBD (gwvbd) event occurs when a gateway has been authorized to manage VBD on its own. When gwvbd is negotiated and VBD stimulus is detected, the gateway reports the event to the Call Agent. The event occurs at four points: start (procedure initiated), update (procedure modified, such as detecting new stimulus), stop (procedure ended successfully), and failure (procedure ended abnormally).

The No Negotiated Procedure for VBD (nopvbd) event handles cases where VBD stimulus is detected but no procedure was negotiated in advance. The gateway may still apply local handling such as adjusting gain, disabling voice activity detection, or switching codecs. The Call Agent may need to issue follow-up commands.

The General-Purpose Media Descriptor (GPMD) package provides a LocalConnectionOption to authorize negotiation of codec-specific modes using the V.152 General-Purpose Media Descriptor Parameter. This allows extending VBD beyond fax and modem to other codec-specific operations.
sections.eli5: The VBD package tells the phone gateway: 'You can handle fax sounds on your own' (gwvbd) or 'I detected fax sounds but we didn't plan for them' (nopvbd). The GPMD package adds a way to authorize special modes for any codec.

sections.title: Event Details and Reason Codes
sections.content:
When a gwvbd event is reported, the gateway includes optional parameters. The reason code (rc) identifies what triggered the switch: CNG (T.30 fax calling), V21flag (fax answering), various modem tone indicators like ANS or Belltone, or payload type switch (PTSW). The codec parameter names the MIME type of the data mode (e.g., audio/PCMU, audio/RED with redundancy, or the target codec on stop such as audio/G729 or image/t38). The coordination technique indicates how the other gateway knows to switch: v152ptsw (payload type switching) or v150fw (V.150.1 state signaling events). The direction parameter notes whether the stimulus came from the GSTN (telephone network) side or the IP side.

With start and update, reason codes indicate what triggered the VBD initiation (fax, modem, or text tones). With stop, reason codes indicate why it ended: SIL (silence), Voice (voice returned), PTSW (payload type switch), or MC (media change to a different type or codec). With failure, only a timeout (TO) reason is defined.

Call Agents must handle unknown parameters gracefully and may remove notification requests after receiving repeated events to avoid notification floods, especially for interspersed text and speech scenarios.
sections.eli5: The event comes with tags saying why it happened (which tone?), what codec it's using, how it's coordinating with the other end, and which direction the tones came from. On stop, it says what ended it: silence, voice returning, switching payload types, or changing to a different media.

sections.title: Integration with Other Packages
sections.content:
The VBD package works alongside existing MGCP packages. The Media Format Parameter (FM) package can be used to authorize redundancy (RFC 2198) with VBD: a call agent can set LocalConnectionOptions with 'fmtp' to specify RED (redundant encoding) MIME subtype details, identifying which redundancy levels and media formats apply. This protects against packet loss during modem or fax transmission.

The FM package is also used with Forward Error Correction (FEC, RFC 5109), allowing a call agent to authorize FEC modes alongside VBD. The RFC notes interaction details: how LocalConnectionOptions and RemoteConnectionDescriptor changes coordinate these techniques.

The Fax package (FXR, RFC 5347) handles T.38 fax relay, which operates on the image/t38 media type. The VBD package can precede it: for example, when CED (called terminal identification) is detected, gwvbd starts; when V.21 flags are detected later, a T.38 transition via FXR is initiated. The VBD procedure stops as a consequence of the media change, with gwvbd reporting a stop event with rc=MC and the new codec (image/t38).
sections.eli5: Other MGCP packages handle redundancy to prevent data loss and T.38 fax relay for better fax transmission. The VBD package coordinates with them: it reports what's happening so the other packages can do their jobs.

sections.title: Call Flow Examples
sections.content:
The RFC provides two detailed call flows. The first is a modem call with gateway-controlled VBD. A Call Agent sets up a connection with gwvbd event notification requested. When the gateway detects ANS (modem answering tone), it reports vbd/gwvbd(start, rc=ANS) and autonomously handles the transition to modem data mode using G.711. The Call Agent refrains from media instructions while the procedure is active. When data transmission completes (silence detected), the gateway reports vbd/gwvbd(stop, rc=SIL) and returns to normal audio mode.

The second flow involves a fax call with gateway-controlled VBD transitioning to T.38 fax relay. The gateway detects CED (fax calling tone), reports vbd/gwvbd(start, rc=CED) and begins VBD. The Call Agent monitors. When V.21 flags are detected, the Call Agent initiates a T.38 transition via a ModifyConnection command with media type image/t38. The gateway confirms with a t38(start) event and simultaneously ends the VBD procedure with vbd/gwvbd(stop, rc=MC). This demonstrates coordination between gateway-controlled and call-agent-controlled procedures.
sections.eli5: One example: phone rings, gateway hears modem tone, tells the call boss, handles the modem data on its own, then reports when it's done. Another example: phone hears fax tone, gateway starts handling it, then the call boss says 'switch to T.38', and the gateway does both at once.
